title: Tlapanec language - Wikipedia
text: Tlapanec / ˈtlæpənɛk /, or Meꞌphaa, is an indigenous Mexican language spoken by more than 98,000 Tlapanec people in the state of Guerrero. [2] Like other Oto-Manguean languages, it is tonal and has complex inflectional morphology.

text: The Oto-Manguean or Otomanguean (/ ˌoʊtoʊˈmæŋɡiːən / OH-to-MANG-ghee-ən) languages are a large family comprising several subfamilies of indigenous languages of the Americas.

title: The sounds of Me'phaa (Tlapanec): A new assessment

title: The tone system of Acatepec Me'paa | SIL Global
text: The tone system of Me'phaa, an Otomanguean language (or group of languages) spoken in the eastern part of the state of Guerrero, Mexico, is quite complex, largely due to the complex agreement systems used with nouns and verbs.
